system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review:** The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and efficiency note do not establish Buyer agreement or remove issues from review. Recommendations below are proposed Buyer positions, based on the supplied summaries—not verification of the underlying DD documents.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at 20%: **AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful general warranty recourse, with separate protection for higher-risk categories. | **Counter at 50% (AUD 12m)**, reserving category carve-outs; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed AUD 25,000; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated; the proposed combined thresholds materially erode recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | Notice within 18 months; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least 24 months for general warranties, with separate category-specific periods and properly preserved notified claims. | **Seek 24 months and reject blanket application**; 18 months may not expose issues across two full reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate protection covering capacity, ownership, valid share issuance and absence of encumbrances. | **Seek a 100%-of-price cap, no thresholds and the applicable statutory limitation period**, subject to the fraud carve-out; core ownership risk should not receive ordinary warranty treatment. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | No express fraud exception supplied; limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | An express exception for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation or concealment, including relevant attributable conduct, and preservation of non-excludable rights. | **Require the exception across every cap, threshold, time bar, disclosure, knowledge and remedy restriction**; contractual protections must not shield fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; a fixed, preserved disclosure record. | **Reject blanket disclosure and require specific, adequately detailed warranty disclosures**; document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge and anything discoverable from data room or public records. | No knowledge exclusion; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer personnel, without enquiry or adviser imputation. | **Delete constructive and imputed knowledge**, and keep specific indemnities unaffected; discoverability is not informed acceptance of risk. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. No final consent or satisfaction evidence supplied. | A Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring effective consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions without unacceptable amendments. | **Require final consent and evidence of all associated conditions before Completion**, with termination rights at the longstop; approximately 30% of FY26 revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Repayment through the completion funds flow and effective release of all relevant security and guarantees at Completion. | **Require a lender payout letter, controlled repayment and binding release mechanics at Completion**, allowing only administrative filings afterwards; debt-free/cash-free delivery cannot depend on an unsecured post-closing promise. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller-funded transaction bonuses plus applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with conditions verified. | **Include the full applicable liability as Seller transaction costs/debt-like items or a separate Seller payment, without double counting**; transaction-triggered remuneration should not reduce the Buyer’s acquired value. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 recorded open, without verified payment or assignment. | Verified payment and effective ownership/assignment of relevant IP, plus protection against resulting title, use and third-party claim risks. | **Require pre-completion cure and broaden the specific indemnity beyond the unpaid fee, outside general limitations**; paying an invoice alone may not establish the complete IP rights the business needs. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary and said not to be material; access, scope, notification obligations and loss remain uncertain. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment, legally required notifications and protection for pre-completion incident liabilities. | **Require an investigation/remediation covenant and specific indemnity outside general warranty limits, supported by appropriate retention**; uncertainty is not evidence of immateriality or a confirmed notifiable breach. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assessment of the **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, timing, enforceability, termination rights, accruals and ordinary-course status. | **Review DD-008 and DD-011 together and control further commitments pending agreement**; any price adjustment must follow the agreed mechanics, not an unsupported assumption that all renewals are ordinary course or debt-like. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance extend to all Claims. | Express, distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and purchase-price/debt obligations. | **Redraft definitions and every cross-reference to preserve category-specific treatment**; an “all Claims” provision could silently override negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Harbourglass as 100% holder. | Independent verification of issued capital, ownership chain, encumbrances, options and other rights, plus valid transfer deliverables. | **Reconcile corporate records and capital documents, conduct relevant searches and obtain clean-title warranties and releases**; a share register is important evidence, not complete proof of unencumbered ownership. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP treated as settled under the general regime. | A separate pre-completion tax indemnity and tailored tax limitations; comprehensive IP ownership/use warranties and appropriate longer protection. | **Reopen both: seek tax protection through relevant assessment periods plus a buffer, and longer/higher-cap IP protection, preserving Ironquay separately**; these risks can crystallise after the general warranty period and exceed its cap. |

**Completion priorities:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment/releases, Ironquay ownership cure, and a corrected funds flow. Do not treat disclosure of these matters as agreement to bear their economic consequences.
=== END ADVICE ===
